source: MEASURED 2026-10-08: real SDK 2.71.0 + Node 22.22.3 real fetch against a local server that writes the header at once and three 1000-byte chunks 200 ms apart (logs/stage-03/survey/probe-stream.mjs, cases stream-wire and convert-header-first). The header NAMES character-cost / request-id are VERBATIM from https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/introduction (accessed 2026-10-08), where they are shown for convert(); that /stream sends character-cost too is NOT documented (openapi declares no response headers for either path) - GUESS until the smoke check. The 200 content type 'audio/mpeg' is from the openapi response of /stream; header VALUES and bytes are COMPOSED.

headers.character-cost: 12   <- GUESS that /stream sends it (documented for convert only)

sdkResult.data: web ReadableStream<Uint8Array>; for await (const chunk of data) yields each chunk as it arrives (MEASURED: no buffering by the SDK)

convertToo.note: MEASURED for O16: convert().withRawResponse() ALSO resolves at the header (4 ms) while its body finished at 405 ms; character-cost was readable at resolve time. So speak can read the billed count before it reads the body.

expect.chunks: Each chunk is a slice of ONE encoded file in the requested output_format (mp3 frames / raw pcm samples). Concatenating all chunks gives what convert() would have returned (GUESS: same bytes; ElevenLabs does not promise byte identity between the two endpoints). Chunk boundaries are arbitrary (TCP), not frame-aligned - GUESS for mp3 frame alignment, not documented.
expect.usage: Billing unit characters; if /stream sends character-cost (smoke check), it is known at the header, BEFORE any audio - so a stream that fails or is aborted later still has its billed count.
expect.mediaType: From the requested format, as speak does.
